## TLDR
Removing container checkout admission could expose host-file links if legacy container terminals remained attachable. The product specification explicitly retires these terminals.

## Details
The patch removes containerized from FileLinks construction and removes asynchronous checkoutLinks admission in provider.row, offering OSC and prose paths directly. Could-be-highest: yes, if a retired container terminal could still expose an out-of-container host file through this path. Proposed bucket: highest only with that missing route; no established shipped security consequence yet. Confidence: source-confirmed removal; acceptance currently rests on the specification pending caller checks. proposed_drop: SPEC.md at this revision, lines 4818–4823: ‘The earlier experimental model, whose supervisor stayed outside the container and bind-mounted a host checkout, is retired. Existing sessions support Delete only. Opening terminals or tabs, exec, Stop, Restart, Clone, Replace and Replace with are refused.’ The new disposable-environment model must still be checked for ordinary in-container supervisor filesystem ownership. possible_cover: none; excluded coverage sources were not read. Next source checks: terminal spec producers and attachment admission for retired sessions, plus new environment host semantics. No execution or reproduction performed.

Reviewed commit: 04d85f0c98a9b635709d00b056719a0baa7fd3fc

## TLDR
Removing the old container checkout filter would expose host-file targets if those terminals remained attachable. Source and specification both retire those terminals; new container sessions use their own supervisor inside the container.

## Details
The patch removes containerized from FileLinks construction and asynchronous checkoutLinks filtering from provider.row. Could-be-highest: yes: without retirement, an old supervisor-outside container terminal could offer host files outside its bind-mounted checkout. Proposed bucket: no report; the potentially highest consequence is refuted for supported current sessions. Confidence: confirmed by source and contract, not execution. proposed_drop: SPEC.md:4818–4823 at this revision says exactly: ‘The earlier experimental model, whose supervisor stayed outside the container and bind-mounted a host checkout, is retired. Existing sessions support Delete only. Opening terminals or tabs, exec, Stop, Restart, Clone, Replace and Replace with are refused.’ Source checks: session_view.rs:3723–3734 keep_terminal_surface immediately returns false for a retired container; service/handlers.rs:1525–1528 rejects attachment through require_active_launch before resolve_terminal or takeover; service/core.rs:3731–3739 rejects launches identified by container::is_retired. SPEC_impl.md:6408–6414 states: ‘Every environment runs an ordinary supervisor’ and ‘The supervisor has no provider-specific launch, terminal or lifecycle mechanism.’ Its transport contract at 6462–6488 routes Podman exec into the container and runs farhelm internal stdio there, so new container paths are interpreted by that supervisor rather than an external host supervisor. No missing current-route premise remains in this group. An already open pre-upgrade client belongs to the old asset version and is not changed by this patch. possible_cover: none; excluded coverage sources were not read. No execution or reproduction performed. Preserve for independent review because the rejected consequence could have been highest.

event.detail:
Reviewed commit: f560058da19e02716e6f943883a9508b447aff4e

## TLDR
Removing the pending terminal-kind gate could have left a terminal attached to an old run after Restart, or discarded the last readable screen during recovery. Source checks show the independent restart generation and snapshot ownership remain intact.

## Details
Considered the removal of kindPending from sync and mountWhenReady and keepTerm→keepScreen cleanup. Could-be-highest: no established loss-of-work or security route; the considered effect was a blank/stale terminal view, high if present. Confidence: confirmed source refutation. proposed_drop: source refutation, plus SPEC.md:3005–3016 explicitly ends old tmux terminals and makes every current terminal a terminal host. session_view.rs:535–564 use_restart_observation increments mount_generation for every new restart_revision, independent of detail payload retirement; terminal_specs at 1702–1784 assigns that generation to the agent only and tabs gen 0. terminal.js:2863 still rebuilds on path or gen change; thus kindPending is no longer needed to distinguish the removed tmux→host transition. The mount gate at 3190–3230 waits for farhelmPasteSanitizer and all grid helpers; lib.rs:1445,1473–1483,1914–1925 registers and injects those exact assets, and paste-sanitizer.js:37 exports the expected name. runReconnect at 1556–1565 sets keepScreen and captures island.grid before unmount; unmount at 4786–4832 tears down notice/deferred drivers, freezes and moves that same grid when keepScreen is set, and otherwise disposes it. No orphaned keepTerm, stopCopyOnSelect, kindPending, spec.kind or farhelmTermBytes reference remains in terminal.js at this revision (git grep checked). possible_cover: none. No execution or reproduction performed. The checked lifecycle preserves the non-live snapshot required by SPEC.md:3018–3019 and does not change the program's lifecycle.

Reviewed commit: f560058da19e02716e6f943883a9508b447aff4e

## TLDR
A grid constructor failure can be masked by another error during file-link cleanup. This defect already affected direct grid mounts in the parent. A changed test models a safer object shape; g136/l1 owns the changed-test finding.

## Details
Confidence: confirmed by source comparison, not execution. terminal.js:946–947 dereferences getGrid().element; createGridSurface:4302–4315 passes () => created before creation completes; 4356–4358 disposes links on construction failure. FileLinks.dispose at terminal-files.js:641–645 calls clearHover:460–468, which accesses the getter even when created remains undefined. This masks the original construction error and stops that cleanup early. Could-be-highest: no established security or loss-of-work route; bucket other for the established diagnostic/cleanup defect and misleading test, with no demonstrated retained-resource consequence. proposed_drop for a new-production-change finding here: unchanged-source scope. Parent terminal.js:1200–1201 has the same getter, 1369–1373 the same disposer, and 5954–6018 the same preassignment closure and catch. Final source check confirms parent:4658–4662 already calls this createGridSurface for spec.kind === host before constructing its socket, so this was not confined to a retired or unused migration path. The full terminal-files.js diff changes comments and removes the old adapter; the relevant clearHover and FileLinks.dispose bodies do not change. Current createGridSurface also runs before its socket at terminal.js:3389–3394. The rewritten terminal-files.test.js fixture at 671–678 always has host and returns host.element, making absent-element disposal safe; test/docstring at 834–844 claims the before-component lifecycle. This changed test is not in g079's assigned grid-buffer.test.js comment patch. possible_cover: parent-supplied g136/l1, independently corroborated by these source checks; no coverage files searched. This closes the lead as a scope record, not as certification that rollback is safe. c2 remains limited to restart/snapshot ownership after successful construction and helper readiness. No unresolved premise for this scope decision, no runtime reproduction, and no drop accepted by the parent.

This should remain distinct from supplied g182/c1, which reports the separately changed browser test's two-column rationale. proposed_drop: not yet; production's correct fit does not by itself refute a newly stale explanation. possible_cover: none for this comment; g182/c1 is adjacent context only. No reproduction or runtime tests.

event.summary: Renderer removal leaves hidden-pane rationale pointing at removed FitAddon
event.detail:
Reviewed commit: f560058da19e02716e6f943883a9508b447aff4e

## TLDR
The intermediate grid-only release still explains hidden terminal sizing through a component it has removed. Its zero-column explanation does not describe the grid's retained-size/no-proposal behavior, giving maintainers the wrong model for the visibility rule. A later assigned commit corrects it.

## Details
At app.css:8571–8580 the rationale for visibility rather than display:none still says ‘FitAddon.fit() would size an unselected terminal to zero columns’. This commit removes the FitAddon asset registration and injection from lib.rs (VENDOR_FIT_JS) and removes its construction/use from terminal.js, leaving no FitAddon runtime for this comment to describe. SPEC_impl.md:1835–1865 defines the replacement as the grid's deterministic fit, not an add-on. Actual grid-terminal.js:462–496 documents that an unmeasurable container proposes nothing and returns before assigning fitted on nonfinite dimensions; :161 and :404–407 initialize that retained size to 80x24. Production sizing can be correct while this independent maintenance explanation remains stale. Fix direction was in fact implemented later: 61e632323dbc6b4a35ed27bf5b9833102ffd5a4e app.css:8571–8575 changes the rationale to the grid being unable to propose a fit without a layout box. The discovery finding is therefore historical/intermediate and does not request another fix at the pinned endpoint.

Whole-range attribution checked: exclusive base 6e423e30068b62c6cfa276c6d720ee35bb70387a app.css:8630–8634 and immediate parent app.css:8611–8615 already contain this sentence, but both still ship and invoke FitAddon. f560058 removes that live referent while preserving the rationale in its assigned stylesheet. The claim that zero columns accurately described the old add-on is not newly validated or asserted here; the in-range defect is failing to replace the explanation when that implementation is removed. This is distinct from supplied g182/c1's separately changed test comment about a two-column floor. Suggested bucket: other, internal documentation accuracy only. Could-be-highest: no established or suspected security/loss-of-work route from this comment. Confidence: confirmed through introducing removal, current and base source, replacement contract and later corrective patch; no execution. proposed_drop: false for the reviewed intermediate revision. possible_cover: source-confirmed correction at 61e632323dbc6b4a35ed27bf5b9833102ffd5a4e, within the assigned range; no prohibited coverage sources searched. No missing premise or runtime reproduction.
